metadata.description: Medical case studies for training diagnostic reasoning and clinical decision-making
metadata.disclaimer: EDUCATIONAL USE ONLY. Not for actual medical diagnosis. All cases are fictional. Consult licensed healthcare professionals for medical advice.

clinical_cases.history_of_present_illness: Patient reports 2 hours of substernal chest pressure, radiating to left arm and jaw. Describes pain as 'heavy weight on chest,' 7/10 severity. Associated with diaphoresis and nausea. Pain began while shoveling snow. Not relieved by rest. Denies shortness of breath or palpitations.
past_medical_history: Former smoker (quit 5 years ago, 30 pack-year history)

physical_exam.cardiovascular: Tachycardic, regular rhythm, no murmurs/rubs/gallops, no JVD
physical_exam.respiratory: Clear to auscultation bilaterally, no wheezes/crackles

initial_workup.ecg: ST-segment elevation 2mm in leads II, III, aVF; reciprocal ST depression in leads I, aVL

supporting_evidence: Classic anginal symptoms (substernal pressure radiating to arm/jaw)
ST elevation in inferior leads (II, III, aVF)
Multiple cardiac risk factors (HTN, DM, smoking history, hyperlipidemia)
critical_next_steps: Activate cardiac catheterization lab immediately (door-to-balloon time <90 min)
Administer dual antiplatelet therapy (aspirin 325mg + P2Y12 inhibitor)
Consider thrombolytic therapy if PCI not available within 120 minutes

differential_diagnosis.probability: Low (ruled out by ST elevation and troponin)

against: ST elevation pattern is localized (not diffuse)

diagnostic_reasoning.most_likely_diagnosis: Inferior STEMI (likely right coronary artery occlusion)

immediate: Call cardiology - activate cath lab for emergent PCI
management_plan.hospital_course: Emergent cardiac catheterization showing 100% occlusion of proximal RCA. Successful PCI with drug-eluting stent placement. Post-procedure troponin peak at 28 ng/mL. Echo shows mild inferior wall hypokinesis, EF 50%.
discharge_plan: Dual antiplatelet therapy (aspirin + ticagrelor) x 12 months
Strict risk factor modification: diet, exercise, smoking cessation maintenance

learning_points: STEMI is a time-critical emergency - door-to-balloon time <90 minutes
Inferior STEMI (II, III, aVF) suggests RCA occlusion
Always check right-sided leads (V4R) in inferior STEMI to assess RV involvement
Classic STEMI presentation: substernal pressure, radiation, diaphoresis, nausea
Risk factors accumulate: HTN + DM + smoking + hyperlipidemia significantly increase risk

clinical_cases.presenting_complaint: 32-year-old female with fatigue, weight gain, and cold intolerance
clinical_cases.history_of_present_illness: 6-month history of progressive fatigue, 15-pound weight gain despite normal appetite, feeling cold when others are comfortable, constipation, dry skin, and hair loss. Also reports irregular menstrual periods and difficulty concentrating at work. Denies heat intolerance, palpitations, or tremor.
clinical_cases.family_history: Mother with 'thyroid problems' (patient unsure of details), maternal aunt with Type 1 Diabetes

physical_exam.general: Appears stated age, mildly overweight, speaks slowly
physical_exam.heent: Dry skin, thinning of lateral eyebrows, no exophthalmos
physical_exam.neck: Thyroid slightly enlarged, diffusely firm, no nodules
physical_exam.extremities: Delayed relaxation phase of deep tendon reflexes, trace pretibial edema

supporting_evidence: Classic symptoms: fatigue, weight gain, cold intolerance, constipation, dry skin, hair loss
Elevated TSH with low free T4 (confirms primary hypothyroidism)
Positive TPO and thyroglobulin antibodies (indicates autoimmune etiology)
Physical exam: delayed DTRs, bradycardia, thyroid enlargement
Family history of autoimmune thyroid disease

against: TSH is elevated (would be low/normal in secondary hypothyroidism)
Objective findings: elevated TSH, low T4, positive antibodies, specific hypothyroid symptoms

diagnostic_reasoning.most_likely_diagnosis: Primary Hypothyroidism due to Hashimoto's Thyroiditis

treatment: Levothyroxine 50 mcg daily (starting dose for young, otherwise healthy patient)
Recheck TSH and free T4 in 6-8 weeks
Titrate levothyroxine by 12.5-25 mcg increments until TSH normalized
Goal TSH: 0.5-2.5 mIU/L for reproductive-age women
Take medication on empty stomach, 30-60 min before breakfast
Avoid taking with calcium, iron supplements, or PPIs (affects absorption)
monitoring: Monitor for symptoms of over-replacement (palpitations, anxiety, weight loss)
Repeat lipid panel after TSH normalized (hypothyroidism can cause hyperlipidemia)
patient_education: Lifelong thyroid hormone replacement likely necessary
Symptoms should improve in 2-4 weeks, fully resolve in 3-6 months
Maintain consistent medication brand if possible

learning_points: Hashimoto's is the most common cause of hypothyroidism in iodine-sufficient areas
TSH is the best screening test for primary thyroid disorders
Classic hypothyroid symptoms: fatigue, weight gain, cold intolerance, constipation, dry skin
Delayed DTR relaxation phase is a specific physical exam finding
Start levothyroxine conservatively and titrate based on TSH
Hypothyroidism can cause reversible hyperlipidemia and anemia

diagnostic_reasoning_exercises.scenario: 45-year-old female with polyuria, polydipsia, and fatigue. Random glucose: 285 mg/dL. What additional tests do you order?
expected_workup: Fasting glucose or HbA1c to confirm diabetes diagnosis
Basic metabolic panel (check for DKA: glucose, electrolytes, anion gap)
Consider: GAD65 and IA-2 antibodies (if suspecting Type 1 vs Type 2)
Consider: C-peptide level (assess endogenous insulin production)
diagnostic_reasoning_exercises.diagnostic_criteria: Diabetes diagnosed if: fasting glucose ≥126 mg/dL, random glucose ≥200 mg/dL with symptoms, or HbA1c ≥6.5%
